chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad narrated to me; he said: My father narrated from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ibrahim ibn Ishaq, from Abdullah ibn Hammad, from Abi Basir, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said:
Recite often: Subhanallah, Alhamdulillah, La ilaha illallah, Allahu Akbar, for indeed they will come on the Day of Resurrection with precedents and followers, and they are the enduring good deeds.

key_terms.وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ: And all praise is due to God
key_terms.وَلَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ: And there is no god but God

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of reciting the four Tasbih phrases frequently according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this hadith in *Thawab al-A'mal*, emphasizing the eschatological weight of the four frequent declarations (Tasbihat al-Arba) as intercessors on the Day of Judgment. In Shia tradition, these phrases are identified with the 'Enduring Good Deeds' (Al-Baqiyat al-Salihat) mentioned in the Quran, serving as spiritual precedents and followers that accompany the believer's soul. This narration underscores the practical importance of consistent dhikr as a means of securing divine mercy and continuous reward beyond the grave.
